ACEMENT AND GRID REPAIR/REPLACEMENT SERVICES 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION 1.1 Background The Federal Government requires professional facility support services to maintain safe, functional, and aesthetically appropriate interior environments across its real property inventory. Over time, suspended acoustic ceiling systems degrade due to building movement, humidity, utility maintenance access, and general wear. To preserve facility integrity, professional intervention is required to repair or in some cases replace structural grid suspension systems and replace all ceiling tiles due to them not matching, being damaged, stained, or missing. 1.2 Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, transportation, and non-personal services necessary to perform ceiling grid repair, alignment, and acoustic ceiling tile replacement services as defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS). The work includes, but is not limited to: - Conducting pre-work inspections of ceiling systems. - Identifying and repairing damaged, bent, or misaligned ceiling grid members (tees and mains). - Securing and leveling the suspension grid system, including replacing or adding hanger wires. - Replace grid that has sustained damage by being bent

he 3rd floor ceiling tile and match the same brand, style, and color. - Legally dispose of all old ceiling tiles and ceiling tile grid offsite. Trash needs to be removed from the worksite daily. - Coordinating work around existing utility fixtures (HVAC diffusers, lighting fixtures, fire sprinklers, and life safety sensors). - New ceiling tile and grid must be stored offsite and only brought to the worksite to be installed the same day. - Enforcing strict adherence to federal, state, and local safety regulations, specifically including OSHA standards and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1). 1.3 Period of Performance The Period of Performance shall be 26 October, 2026 - 31 January, 2027 1.4 Place of Performance The services shall be performed at Naval Station Norfolk, Building Number W143, and 9550 Decatur Avenue, Norfolk, VA23511. 1.5 Work Hours and Federal Holidays - Normal Work Hours: All work shall be performed between the hours of 0700 and 1600, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Holidays, unless otherwise approved by the COR. - Federal Holidays: The Contractor is not required to perform routine services on the following federal holidays: - New Year's Day - Martin Luther K

It typically consists of an external socket or frame that fits over the arm and interfaces with a prosthetic hand or terminal device (e.g., TASKA CX hand). Bypass prostheses are commonly used for research, training, and demonstration purposes, enabling clinicians, engineers, and study participants to evaluate prosthetic technologies, control strategies, and user performance without requiring an amputation. Bypass prostheses can be configured in different geometries depending on the intended use. In one configuration, the prosthetic hand is mounted as a direct extension of the intact limb, resulting in a longer overall limb length that extends beyond the natural hand. In another configuration, the device incorporates an angled offset, positioning the terminal device so that it aligns more closely with the length and functional position of the intact limb. Critical to this acquisition is the use of “brand name or equal” when describing specific components and their salient performance characteristics in this RFQ.
